shape.text: A Composio project API key begins with ak_. The provider's authentication documentation and its SDK source name the prefix, and the documentation names the x-api-key request header that carries the key.

The body is exactly 20 characters. A dated statement by Composio's Head of Security (2026-09-17, posted on a public scanner issue) gives ak_ plus 20 nanoid characters, and the provider's OpenAPI example shows an ak_ key with a 20-character body.

The body is a URL-safe nanoid drawn from letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, so a body may begin or end with an underscore or a hyphen. The keys use an underscore-separated scheme with no checksum and no further separators.
The key has no separators and no checksum.

unresolved.reason: The statement that no checksum exists is held in a contract claim that is itself unresolved; it rests on one staff comment and no provider specification.

collisions.text: The prefix ak_ is short and the alphabet includes the underscore and hyphen, so a 20-character snake_case identifier can look like a project key. Requiring at least one uppercase and one lowercase letter in the body would rule most of these out, at a cost of about 3 in 100,000 genuine keys on each side.
